<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">📌 Overview</h2><a id="user-content--overview" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: 📌 Overview" href="#-overview"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">What truly drives student academic performance? This project investigates how daily lifestyle habits — study time, sleep, diet, exercise, social media usage, and mental health — relate to students' exam scores using a rigorous, statistics-driven approach.</p>
<p dir="auto">The analysis follows a structured five-stage workflow:</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Data Quality Assessment → Univariate Profiling → Bivariate Analysis → Statistical Hypothesis Testing → Predictive Modeling</strong></p>
<p dir="auto">All findings are validated with proper statistical tests (p-values, effect sizes) and summarized in an interactive Power BI dashboard designed for non-technical stakeholders.</p>
<blockquote>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Thesis Project</strong> | 1,000 student records | 16 features | 9 statistical tests | Python EDA + Power BI Dashboard</p>
</blockquote>
<hr>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">🎯 Objective & Research Questions</h2><a id="user-content--objective--research-questions" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: 🎯 Objective & Research Questions" href="#-objective--research-questions"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>Primary:</strong> Which behavioral factors have a <em>statistically significant</em> impact on exam performance?</li>
<li><strong>Secondary:</strong> Can a small set of habit-based features reliably predict academic outcomes?</li>
<li><strong>Stakeholders:</strong> Students (behavior optimization), Educators (early-risk identification), Institutions (resource allocation)</li>

<p dir="auto">To validate bivariate findings and quantify explained variance:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>Algorithm:</strong> Linear Regression via sklearn Pipeline</li>
<li><strong>Preprocessing:</strong> <code>ColumnTransformer</code> — passthrough for numericals, <code>OneHotEncoder(drop='first')</code> for categoricals</li>
<li><strong>Split:</strong> 80/20 train-test (<code>random_state=42</code>)</li>
<li><strong>Metrics:</strong> R², MAE, baseline MAE (predicting mean) for comparison</li>
<li><strong>Feature Importance:</strong> Coefficient analysis with directional interpretation (positive/negative effect)</li>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto"><g-emoji class="g-emoji" alias="warning">⚠️</g-emoji> Limitations</h2><a id="user-content-️-limitations" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: ⚠️ Limitations" href="#️-limitations"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<ol dir="auto">
<li>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Cross-sectional & self-reported data:</strong> Causal direction cannot be established. For example, does poor mental health cause low scores, or do low scores worsen mental health? Longitudinal data would be needed to answer this.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Uniform marginal distributions:</strong> All features exhibit near-zero skewness and negative kurtosis, suggesting the dataset may be partially synthetic. This could explain why some traditionally strong predictors (sleep, attendance) show weaker-than-expected correlations. Findings should be confirmed on real-world data before generalizing.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Baseline model only:</strong> The Linear Regression model captures linear relationships but may miss non-linear interactions (e.g., <code>study_hours × mental_health</code>). Tree-based models (Random Forest, XGBoost) could improve predictive performance.</p>
</li>
</ol>
